title: Quick-Commerce Deductions
summary: Match every Blinkit, Zepto and Swiggy Instamart payment back to its POs, invoices and dark-store receipts, check each deduction against your agreed terms, and dispute the wrong ones.

seo.title: Quick-Commerce Deductions Reconciliation | VipraTech
seo.description: Reconcile Blinkit, Zepto and Swiggy Instamart payments with POs, invoices and GRNs, check every deduction against agreed terms and dispute wrong ones.

problem.intro: Brands that sell to quick-commerce platforms ship against hundreds of purchase orders a month to warehouses and dark stores. What comes back is a payment that is less than the invoices, with deductions for short receipts, damage and near-expiry rejections, margin differences, promotion support and other charges, explained across portal reports and remittance files.

pain_points.title: Payments that never add up
pain_points.detail: One payment covers many invoices and many deductions, so finance cannot see which invoice was short-paid or why without days of spreadsheet work.

pain_points.title: Receiving-dock deductions
pain_points.detail: Short receipts, damage and near-expiry rejections are raised at the dark store or warehouse, and the brand rarely has the evidence to check them.

pain_points.title: Terms applied inconsistently
pain_points.detail: Margins, promotion support and charges are agreed per platform and per SKU, but deductions are not checked against what was actually agreed.

pain_points.title: Dispute windows close
pain_points.detail: Each platform has its own process and deadline for disputes, and the wrong deductions that nobody had time to raise are written off.

solution.overview: VipraTech brings together purchase orders, your invoices, each platform's receipt and return reports, payment advice and the trade terms you agreed with each platform. It reads portal exports and remittance files in each platform's format, ties every payment back to the invoices it covers, classifies each deduction and checks it against the receipt evidence and the agreed terms. Deductions that hold up are accepted. The rest are flagged with the reason and the evidence, and finance decides which to dispute. The system then builds a dispute pack in the platform's format and tracks what is recovered.
capabilities: Reads portal exports, payment advice and remittance files from each platform
Ties every payment to the invoices and purchase orders it covers
Classifies deductions: short receipt, damage, expiry, rate difference, promotion and other charges
Checks each deduction against receipt evidence and the terms agreed with that platform
Builds dispute packs with the evidence attached and tracks recoveries
Ageing report of open deductions and disputes by platform

workflow.title: Collect documents
workflow.detail: POs, invoices, receipt and return reports, and payment advice are pulled from portals, email and your ERP for the period.

workflow.title: Normalise
workflow.detail: Each platform's files are read into one structure of PO, invoice, SKU, quantity, amount and deduction.

workflow.title: Tie payments to invoices
workflow.detail: Every payment is matched to the invoices it covers, and every short payment is split into its deductions.

workflow.title: Check each deduction
workflow.detail: Deductions are checked against receipt evidence and the terms agreed with that platform.

workflow.title: Finance review
workflow.detail: Finance reviews flagged deductions with the reason and evidence, and decides which to dispute.

workflow.title: Dispute and track
workflow.detail: Dispute packs are prepared in each platform's format, and recoveries are tracked to closure.

match_rules.logic: Every invoice must be paid in full or carry a deduction that explains the difference.
A shortage deduction must match the gap between invoiced and received quantity on the GRN for that PO and dark store.
Rate deductions are checked against the PO price and the margin agreed for that date.
Fill-rate and other penalties must follow the formula and thresholds in your trade agreement for that period.
Listing, visibility and marketing fees must match an agreed plan or a platform invoice.

exception_codes.meaning: The shortage is not supported by the GRN.
exception_codes.action: Dispute, with the GRN and delivery proof.

exception_codes.meaning: The deduction applies a rate below the PO price.
The penalty does not follow the agreement's formula.
A fee has no agreed plan behind it.
exception_codes.action: Check with the key account manager, then dispute.

exception_codes.meaning: A short payment has no debit note or reason.
exception_codes.action: Ask the platform for the debit note.

inputs: Your invoices from the ERP or Tally
Receipt, short-receipt, damage and return reports
Trade terms, margins and promotion agreements for each platform
outputs: Classified deductions with the evidence for each
List of deductions to dispute, with reasons
Dispute packs in each platform's format
Ageing report of open deductions and recoveries
human_in_the_loop: Finance decides which deductions to accept and which to dispute. The system never raises a dispute on its own, and any deduction it cannot match to evidence or terms is flagged for a person rather than accepted.
integrations: Bank statements and payment advice by email
ERP such as SAP or Tally for invoices and receipts
guardrails: No deduction accepted without matching evidence or agreed terms
Every flagged deduction shows its reason and source documents
Disputes are raised only after finance approves them
Terms are versioned by platform and date
compliance_notes: Deductions that change the value of a supply, such as rate differences or returns, may need a credit or debit note for GST. The system keeps the link between deduction, invoice and note that your tax team needs.
TDS deducted on payments can be matched to Form 26AS so that credits are not missed.

rollout.scope: One platform, using the last two to three months of POs, invoices, receipt reports and payments, with deductions finance has already reviewed as the benchmark.
deliverables: Parsers for the platform's reports and payment files
Payment-to-invoice reconciliation for the rollout period
Deduction review queue with reasons and evidence
Dispute pack format agreed with your team

what_we_measure.how: Share of payments tied to their invoices with every deduction explained.
Deductions the system flagged that finance agreed were wrong.
Amount disputed in the rollout period, and the amount recovered so far.
Time from payment receipt to a reconciled, explained payment, compared with today.

faqs.a: It is built around the reports each platform gives you, so it can cover Blinkit, Zepto, Swiggy Instamart and newer platforms. Rollout starts with the platform where you lose the most to deductions. Supermarket and department store chains are covered by modern-trade deductions.

faqs.q: Do you need access to our platform portals?
faqs.a: No. Exports from the portals and the payment files you already receive are enough to start. Automating the downloads can come later, with your approval.

faqs.q: Can it file disputes for us?
faqs.a: It prepares the dispute pack with the evidence attached. Your team approves and submits it, and the system tracks the outcome.

faqs.q: How long does it take to go live?
faqs.a: Two monthly cycles, about 8 weeks from the first files to go-live. The first cycle runs beside your current process on your own data, and your team switches over once the results agree with what it would have settled.
